clue.text: Revolutionary tyre held corner only at first

indicators.note: the tyre word holds the next piece within its letters

parts.note: a radial is a type of car tyre

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word corner is used

explanation.surface: A motorist's tyre gripped the bend only at the start of the turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' puts C, the first letter of 'corner', inside RADIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolutionary is an extremist politician wanting sweeping change, which is a radical.

clue.text: Keep away chorus

explanation.surface: Someone stays clear of the singalong.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to abstain or hold back from something; a refrain is the repeated lines of a song.

clue.text: Grammatically a no-no?

parts.note: read literally, 'no-no' is two negative words together, which grammar teachers forbid as a construction

explanation.surface: Something forbidden by the rules of grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of negatives in one statement, as in 'I don't want none', is frowned on in standard grammar.

clue.text: Fish — a final piece

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish

explanation.surface: A fish served as the last course.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical coda is the closing passage that rounds off a composition.

clue.text: Everyone's chances equal here-it always ends in a draw

definitions.text: Everyone's chances equal here-it always ends in a draw

parts.words: Everyone's chances equal here-it always ends in a draw
parts.note: a draw seems to mean a tied match, but here it is the picking of winning tickets by chance

explanation.surface: A contest where all sides are evenly matched and the result is always a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A game of chance where tickets are bought and winners are picked at random from a drum.

clue.text: Pound of potatoes?

parts.note: pound suggests a weight of vegetables, but here it means crushing them to a pulp

explanation.surface: Asking for a pound weight of spuds at the greengrocer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mashed potato is made by pounding boiled potatoes until smooth.

clue.text: Took up, eg a space, for boat to anchor

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means written from the bottom upwards, so these words read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: Somebody occupied, for example, a berth so their vessel could tie up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took up' turns the run EGA + ROOM so it reads MOOR + AGE; 'for' links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorage is a place where a vessel may be secured or tied up.

clue.text: Nothing to support emergency call? That's not very good

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece placed below holds up the one above it

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: With no one backing up a distress signal, things are looking poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' sets O beneath SOS in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Something middling or mediocre is described as so-so.

clue.text: How to make TV work? Hurry up!

explanation.surface: Someone impatient with a balky television set.
explanation.definitionFit: To get a set going you push its power button down; to push on is also to hurry along.

clue.text: They're young to love the bard's work

definitions.text: They're young to love the bard's work

parts.words: They're young to love the bard's work
parts.note: seems to be about youngsters enjoying Shakespeare, but describes a play of his about two teenage lovers

explanation.surface: Young people who are fans of Shakespeare's writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy of two youthful lovers from feuding Verona families.

clue.text: The first college block?

parts.note: sounds like a first campus building, but is the ceremonial first stone laid for any building

explanation.surface: Asking which hall was the original one on campus.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial stone laid to mark the start of building work on an institution.

clue.text: Take the whole year to find colleague

parts.note: all means the whole of something

explanation.surface: It takes twelve months to make friends with a workmate.
explanation.definitionFit: An associate or partner who stands with you is an ally.

clue.text: Be unprofessional, but stay on board

parts.note: taken as written
lay means not belonging to a profession, as in a lay opinion

explanation.surface: An amateur is told to stay seated on the committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' means aboard ship: belay is a nautical order to stop or to secure a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: In sailing, belay means stop or hold fast, as when making a rope secure on a cleat.

clue.text: County gardens

explanation.surface: A shire full of flower borders.
explanation.definitionFit: Beds is the short form of Bedfordshire, an English county; flower plots in a garden are also beds.

clue.text: Satisfied with the spectacles? So am I!

parts.note: met means satisfied, as when demands are met
two round lenses look like the letters OO

explanation.surface: Someone pleased with their new glasses, and a friend agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: The spectacles are pictured as the letters OO, two round lenses side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply agreeing that the same holds for the speaker as well.

clue.text: Extra thin

explanation.surface: A two-word note about something additional and lean.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare item is a surplus one; a spare figure is lean and slight.

clue.text: Conventional life here for sisters?

parts.note: conventional seems to mean ordinary, but is read as of a convent, where religious sisters live

explanation.surface: Siblings settling for an ordinary existence.
explanation.definitionFit: A house where an order of nuns lives together is a convent.

clue.text: No longer clear-help to understand

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-husband
plain means clear or obvious

explanation.surface: Something once obvious now needs some assistance to grasp.
explanation.definitionFit: To clarify or make something comprehensible to another person is to explain it.

clue.text: In S Africa, almost ignore foreign woman

indicators.note: the shortened word sits inside the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa

indicators.note: the word ignore loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Travelling in South Africa, one nearly ignored a woman from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'S Africa' is a two-word abbreviation; the definition 'foreign woman' covers any lady addressed in Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Signora is the Italian title for a married woman, a lady from abroad to an English speaker.

clue.text: It enables child to put the worries of school behind him

definitions.text: It enables child to put the worries of school behind him

parts.words: It enables child to put the worries of school behind him
parts.note: seems to be about forgetting troubles, but literally the child carries his school things on his back

explanation.surface: Something that helps a pupil forget the stresses of lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolbag with a strap, often worn on the back, for carrying books.

clue.text: Makes real proposal to shorten play?

explanation.surface: A director suggesting cuts to a drama to make it more realistic.
explanation.definitionFit: To act out a fantasy is to perform it for real; a call to remove scenes from a drama would be 'acts out'.

clue.text: Semiprecious stone sacrificed to pride

indicators.note: the letters of to pride are given up and destroyed, then rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A gem given up for the sake of vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: A green gem variety of olivine used in jewellery.

clue.text: Give warning of wine running out?

parts.note: port is a fortified Portuguese wine
to end is to run out or finish

explanation.surface: Raising the alarm that the fortified wine is nearly gone.
explanation.definitionFit: To foretell or presage something, often trouble, is to be an omen of it.

clue.text: Halfway through bird, see new jailer

indicators.note: the next piece goes into the middle of the bird's name

parts.note: the turkey is a large farm bird

explanation.surface: Midway through the poultry, a prison guard is spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Halfway through' sets N after the first three letters of TURKEY; 'see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnkey is an old word for a prison warder who keeps the keys.

clue.text: Bear with the betting system

explanation.surface: Carrying something along to the racecourse betting window.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry; the Tote is the pool betting system at British racecourses.

clue.text: Desolate time in a Channel Island

indicators.note: the time letter goes inside the island's name

parts.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands between England and France

explanation.surface: A bleak spell spent on a small island in the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: SARK is a small car-free Channel Island near Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: A stark landscape is bleak, bare and barren.

clue.text: How we know queen, say, is content?

definitions.text: How we know queen, say, is content?

parts.words: How we know queen, say, is content?
parts.note: the queen seems royal, but is a female cat, whose happy sound shows she is pleased

explanation.surface: Wondering how one can tell the monarch is happy.
explanation.definitionFit: The low rumbling noise a cat makes when pleased.

clue.text: He calls for armour

indicators.note: the word for a man is spoken, giving a word with the same pronunciation

parts.note: he refers to a man, a male

explanation.surface: A man shouts for protective gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calls' signals the sound of a word: the masculine word for He is said, giving the armour word.
explanation.definitionFit: Chain mail is flexible armour of linked metal rings.

clue.text: Back of ironclad, our stern

indicators.note: only the closing letter of ironclad is used

explanation.surface: The rear of our warship is its stern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' looks like the back of the ship but is the adjective meaning severe.
explanation.definitionFit: A dour person is severe, grim and unsmiling.

clue.text: Want to argue over choice of treat for dog?

definitions.text: Want to argue over choice of treat for dog?

parts.words: Want to argue over choice of treat for dog?
parts.note: literally a dog wanting a chew to gnaw at; idiomatically wishing to raise a grievance

explanation.surface: Disputing which snack to give the family pet.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for having a grievance one wishes to discuss with someone.

clue.text: Boring place to live

explanation.surface: A dull apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat performance is dull and lifeless; a flat is an apartment on one floor.

clue.text: Oz girl moving to hydro

indicators.note: the letters of to hydro shift into a new order

explanation.surface: An Australian girl relocating to a hydroelectric plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oz' suggests Australia, but it is the Land of Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of The Wizard of Oz, who travels there from Kansas.
